{"returncode":0,"stdout":"1003: ## 3. The twenty-two prime audits, ordered by what a failure costs
1004:  Every session closes with twenty-two audits. They are not spot checks, and they are not equal. They
1005: 
1006: ### 3.0 Ten of the twenty-two test the index; twelve test the book
1007: 
1008:  **For a reader who wants the index rather than the artefact, ten audits carry the whole of it:**
1009: 
1010:       1·   LATTICE        Λ's cells, closure and defect, recomputed from the construction
1011:       2·   EQUATIONS      the printed identities re-derived — F(1), F(−1), d(x,y), E
1012:       8·   CELL           every cell the text names exists in the index
1013:       9·   DISTINCTNESS   no two index coordinates collapse
1014:       10·  SCOPE          an E value is stated with the index it belongs to
1015:       13·  AGREEMENT      one quantity, one value across the whole work
1016:       14·  ARITHMETIC     the tower's own table against the recomputed tower
1017:       18·  REPRODUCTION   the two headline figures reproduce
1018:       20·  PROJECTION     no claim of predictive power anywhere in the text
1019:       21·  INPUT          every computation names its input set
1020: 
1021:     **These ten would still have to pass if the book were rewritten from scratch in
1022:     another form.** They are about Λ and the objects around it.
1023: 
1024:  **The other twelve test whether this book is a usable artefact** — CONSISTENCY, REDUNDANCY,
1025:  ARTEFACT, COHERENCE, ATTRIBUTION, ANTECEDENT, MARKUP, ENUMERATION, FIDELITY, MEASURE, SEQUENCE and
1026:  CENSUS. **Every one has caught something real**, and several caught faults in this chapter's own
1027:  reconstruction. *But a reader assessing the mathematics does not need to know that a § reference
1028:  resolves or that a figure count matches; those protect the reader from the author.*
1029: 
1030:     **The split is stated rather than enforced. All twenty-two run on every build,
1031:     and the artefact twelve have caught more faults than the index ten** — which is
1032:     the honest reason not to demote them.
1033: 
1034:  **The twenty-two are ordered by the cost of the failure each one catches.**
1035: 
1036:     The first two can make the book WRONG. The next two can make it UNREADABLE AS AN
1037:     ARGUMENT. The next two can make it UNUSABLE AS AN OBJECT. The seventh can make it
1038:     DISHONEST, and it is the only one that cannot be run by reading the book.
1039: 
1040:  1 — LATTICE. Every structural claim recomputed from the construction: closure under join and meet,
1041:  E(X) = 0, rank modularity, the fibre identities, the rank polynomial, F(1) and F(−1), |J(Λ)| and the height.
1042:  Over all 475,800 pairs of Λ, not a sample. First, because if the object is not closed the book has no
1043:  subject.
1044: 
1045:  2 — EQUATIONS. Every equation the book states, evaluated numerically against the data it claims to
1046:  describe. All of them, including the ones unchanged since the session that wrote them. Second,
1047:  because a wrong equation is a false claim.
1048: 
1049:  3 — CONSISTENCY. No two statements in the book may contradict. A claim corrected in one chapter
1050:  must not survive uncorrected in another; a number revised in a table must be revised in the prose that
1051:  cites it. Third, because a contradiction leaves the reader unable to tell which statement is the claim.
1052: 
1053:  4 — REDUNDANCY. No statement may survive its own supersession. Every summary is compared
1054:  against what it summarises; every table against the section it condenses; and any section that only
1055:  restates another is removed rather than maintained. Fourth, because a stale claim is a false claim that
1056:  passed every other check.
1057: 
1058:  5 — ARTEFACT. Audits 1–4 read the SOURCE. This one reads the built PDF. Missing glyphs, figures
1059:  present and non-blank, the title page and running header read back, no table overflowing its frame, the
1060:  whitespace measured from glyph and image geometry, and every figure checked for ink, tone, resolution,
1061:  duplication and correct numbering. Fifth, because the source can be perfect and the page still wrong.
1062: 
1063:  6 — COHERENCE. *Source, other places, unusable, presupposes labels are addressable.* Every
1064:  cross-reference resolves; every figure has a caption and every caption a figure;
1065:  every stated count matches its computation; every principle referred to is defined; and the contents
1066:  block is checked against the actual headings. Last, because these failures cost navigation rather
1067:  than truth — and because it is the only audit that can be run before the others.
1068: 
1069: 7 — ATTRIBUTION. Every claim that points outside the book resolves to a source the book lists, and
1070:  every source listed is claimed by something inside it. Five checks: each work cited in the text
1071:  appears in the References; each entry in the References is cited somewhere; §29.2's owner column
1072:  names people the References carry; every Appendix D element recorded as *precedent found* has a
1073:  reachable citation; and every data source in Appendix B is listed. Seventh, because a missing
1074:  attribution makes the book neither wrong nor unreadable nor unusable — it makes it **dishonest**,
1075:  which is a worse failure and a quieter one.
1076: 
1077:     Audits 1–2 check the book against the world. Audits 3–4 check the book against itself.
1078:     Audits 5–6 check the book against what a reader receives. **Audit 7 checks the book against
1079:     what it owes**, and it is the only one of the seven that cannot be run by reading the book.

1060:  whitespace measured from glyph and image geometry, and every figure checked for ink, tone, resolution,
1061:  duplication and correct numbering. Fifth, because the source can be perfect and the page still wrong.
1062: 
1063:  6 — COHERENCE. *Source, other places, unusable, presupposes labels are addressable.* Every
1064:  cross-reference resolves; every figure has a caption and every caption a figure;
1065:  every stated count matches its computation; every principle referred to is defined; and the contents
1066:  block is checked against the actual headings. Last, because these failures cost navigation rather
1067:  than truth — and because it is the only audit that can be run before the others.
1068: 
1069: 7 — ATTRIBUTION. Every claim that points outside the book resolves to a source the book lists, and
1070:  every source listed is claimed by something inside it. Five checks: each work cited in the text
1071:  appears in the References; each entry in the References is cited somewhere; §29.2's owner column
1072:  names people the References carry; every Appendix D element recorded as *precedent found* has a
1073:  reachable citation; and every data source in Appendix B is listed. Seventh, because a missing
1074:  attribution makes the book neither wrong nor unreadable nor unusable — it makes it **dishonest**,
1075:  which is a worse failure and a quieter one.
1076: 
1077:     Audits 1–2 check the book against the world. Audits 3–4 check the book against itself.
1078:     Audits 5–6 check the book against what a reader receives. **Audit 7 checks the book against
1079:     what it owes**, and it is the only one of the seven that cannot be run by reading the book.
1080:

1082:  §F.3.1 and §E.1.3 remove two counts because a figure computed from the book cannot be printed as
1083:  prose. **Removal is not a repair on its own.** A stale number is wrong; a missing number is not
1084:  therefore right, and deleting one without replacing what it carried loses the reader something the

1087:     **Any figure withdrawn must have its data represented another way** — by the law that generates
1088:     it, by the stable structure beneath it, or by a computation the artefact performs. The
1089:     withdrawal and the replacement are one act.
1090: 
1091:  **Three representations are available and they are not equivalent.**
1092: 
1093:  **By the law.** Best where one exists. §F.3.1 replaces a count with the constraint that generates it —
1094:  *definition = stated forbids inputs = enumerated* — which cannot go stale because it is a fact about
1095:  the assignment rules rather than the text.

1098:  nine combinations admitted and absent in every state of the book, against a count that read five
1099:  different values in one session; §E.1.3 asserts E(Q) = 0 under its fibration, which has held at five
1100:  different item totals.

1103:  press prints E(G), the open count, E(Q) unfibred, the register's span and the withdrawal ratio on
1104:  every build. **These are readouts and are marked as such** — a number the artefact computes about

{"returncode":0,"stdout":"1150:     A closed index is exactly the set its own envelopes admit. §15.2 proves those
1151:     envelopes are recoverable from its cells, so an expression always exists — and
1152:     printing E = 0 without it withholds something the author already has.
1153: 
1154:  **A reader given the verdict must take closure on trust; a reader given the envelopes can rerun
1155:  it.** The difference is §2.18's, between a computable quantity and a decided one, applied to the
1156:  central claim this book makes about every object it builds.
1157: 
1158:  **Audited across the twenty closed indices this work and its companion carry: fourteen state an
1159:  expression, one states a fibration and no expression, and five state a verdict and nothing else** —
1160:  the audits at three coordinates, Q fibred by domain, and the geometry, solution and ANEC-coverage
1161:  indices of the companion paper. Λ states F(z₁…z₈); the tower states its five bounds; the register
1162:  index states the envelope ℛ recovered from it; the back-matter Index states its down-set condition.
1163:  The five that do not are not wrong. **They are unrerunnable**, which is the state §2.18 exists to
1164:  make visible and this protocol exists to forbid. Register 439.
1165: 
1166:     Any register entry that a proof, theorem, equation or expression settles must name that
1167:     object, and the object must name the entry. A reference in one direction is a citation;
1168:     a reference in both is an index.
1169: 
1170:  **Half the register fails this, and the failure is asymmetric.** Of 219 entry-lines carrying 248
1171:  numbers: 66 carry a mathematical object *and* a § reference; **89 carry an object and no reference**;
1172:  35 are mathematical in subject and carry neither; 59 are narrative, settled by no object at all.
1173:  **107 entries are corroborable and not searchable from what corroborates them.**
1174: 
1175:  **And the reverse direction barely exists.** Of the 132 mathematical objects this book states, **four
1176:  cite a register entry.** An entry can sometimes be traced to its mathematics; the mathematics can
1177:  almost never be traced to what it corrected.
1178: 
1179:     A register that cannot be searched from the mathematics is a record of the work and not
1180:     an instrument of it.
1181: 
1182:  Register 415.
1183: 
1184: ### 2.24 Never one heuristic — §2.8, and the one thing it does not say
1185: 
1186:     Where a quantity is reached by a heuristic rather than computed, run at least two
1187:     heuristics of different kind and **report the SPREAD**. A single heuristic cannot
1188:     tell you whether it is in the case where it works.
1189: 
1190:  **The first sentence is §2.8 and this book already had it.** *For every quantity that matters, build
1191:  a second derivation that does not pass through the first* — and the seed is a quantity that matters,
1192:  prune-greedy was one derivation, and no second was ever built. **§2.8's own gloss is what happened:
1193:  an identity computed along one path is vacuous.** The protocol was not missing; it was not applied.
1194: 
1195:  **What §2.24 adds is the SPREAD.** §2.8 asks for agreement between two routes and is satisfied when
1196:  they agree. **A spread of thirty-three around an exact seven is not disagreement about a value — it
1197:  is information about which case you are in**, and §2.8 has no place to put it. That is the whole of
1198:  what is new here.
1199: 
1200:  *Found by indexing the protocols: §2.8 and §2.24 occupy the same cell in every coordinate — trigger,
1201:  object, failure and how each was earned. Register 514.*
1202: 
1203:  **This protocol exists because that failure ran for twelve cycles.** Every seed size in §14.5.7 and
1204:  §14.5.8 came from one algorithm — prune-greedy — and every expression fitted to those sizes was
1205:  checked against numbers from the same source. **The fits could not fail**, which is §4.6's condition
1206:  for a check that is not evidence.
1207: 
1208:  **What the spread shows.** Five heuristics on Λ₈ give 12, 7, 7, 7 and **40**, around an exact seven.
1209:  On a regular down-set they give 7, 7, 7, 7, 7 — and the lower bound is 7 too, so the answer is
1210:  exact. **The spread is zero where the object is regular and thirty-three where it is not**, and no
1211:  single run distinguishes those cases.
1212: 
1213:     **A heuristic's output is a bound. Two heuristics' outputs are a bound and a
1214:     warning. Neither is a value.**
1215: 
1216:  And a lower bound is worth as much as a second heuristic: §14.5.9's disjoint-witness bound is what
1217:  showed the gap between seven and forty was real rather than a tie. Register 506.
1218: 
1219: ### 3.1 Why three of the audits were needed
1220:  CONSISTENCY: twenty-eight cross-references once pointed at a section that had moved. ARTEFACT: a
1221:  rendered page once carried glyphs the source did not. ATTRIBUTION: the three precedents that place
1222:  this book's central theorem in existing literature were cited in the text and absent from the
1223:  References. Each history is in the register — 262, 285, 294 and the grouped mechanisms at §28.7.8.
1224:  **A protocol states what to do; the record states what happened.**
1225:

content.text:
{"returncode":0,"stdout":"1226: ### 3.2 The whitespace clause, and two measurements that were wrong
1227:  A gap a reader sees is a defect the source cannot show. So the audit reads the position of every
1228:  glyph and every image and compares the inked extent with the frame.
1229: 
1230:  On this book: median foot gap 3.3%, nine pages above 15%, worst 31% — and that one is the
1231:  end of a section, where a gap is correct. Interior gaps cluster at 16–28%, which is exactly the
1232:  CondPageBreak(58mm) guard that stops a heading landing at the foot of a page.
1233: 
1234:  Tightening the guard makes it worse, not better. At 46mm the count of gaps falls from nine to
1235:  seven and the worst rises from 31% to 43%, because a heading allowed to sit lower pushes the figure
1236:  block after it off the page entirely. 58mm is the optimum, and it was found by measuring rather
1237:  than by preference.
1238: 
1239: ### 3.3 Exhaustive, and what to do when it is impossible
1240:  Check every cell where the set is finite and small enough. Where it is not, state the sampling and its
1241:  size in the same sentence as the result, and never let a sampled figure stand where an exhaustive one
1242:  is affordable — §16.5 stood on 30,000 samples of a 6,912-cell box until register 248.
1243: 
1244: ### 3.4 And two of the audit's own measurements were wrong first
1245:  The first attempt used the PDF text matrix directly and reported a median inked fraction of 103%
1246:  — impossible — with y-coordinates of 5, 6 and −220. The text matrix is not page geometry until it is
1247:  composed with the current transformation matrix.
1248: 
1249:  The second attempt counted characters and not images, and flagged seven pages as having a
1250:  25–45% gap at the head. All seven begin with a figure. The space was not empty; it was occupied by
1251:  something the measurement could not see.
1252: 
1253:     Both are the same error as the audits they were written to replace: a check looking at the
1254:     wrong artefact. An audit is not exempt from the discipline it enforces, and this one needed two
1255:     corrections before its first clean reading.
1256: 
1257: ### 3.5 What the figure audit found
1258:  Twenty-eight figures, each checked against its caption and its file.
1259: 
1260:  Clean: every figure has a caption and every caption a figure; no image is blank or unusually dark; no file
1261:  is duplicated; nothing in fig/ is unused; and after one correction every figure number matches the
1262:  chapter it sits in.
1263: 
1264:  The one correction. Figures 23.1 and 23.2 appeared in the wrong order — the arity figure sits in §30.3.2
1265:  and the step-law figure in §30.3.4, so the numbering ran backwards against the reading order. Swapped.
1266: 
1267:  And one defect that is recorded rather than repaired.
1268: 
1269:   figures at 300 dpi or better                                                  5
1270:   between 200 and 300                                                           8
1271:   under 200 dpi                                                                 15
1272:   median                                                                        164 dpi
1273: 
1274:  Fifteen figures were produced by an earlier pipeline whose default was figure.dpi = 160, and
1275:  at 163 mm rendered width that gives 140–164 dpi — below print standard. Regenerating them needs
1276:  the source data of the sessions that made them, which this one does not carry. Appendix C.3
1277:  lists them with the rest of what was inherited and not recomputed.
1278: 
1279:     The audit's value here is not that it fixed the figures. It is that the number is now written
1280:     down instead of unknown.
1281: 
1282: ### 3.6 Why the REDUNDANCY audit was needed
1283:  Because two sections survived their own supersession and passed all five.
1284: 
1285:  A summary table listed Q's eight items while Appendix E enumerated, indexed and closed them —
1286:  the same content, maintained twice. And a status table still read "nine literatures entered, nine
1287:  named and unentered" and "order recovery beyond trees: open, and known to be hard", both superseded
1288:  hours earlier by §E.5 and §30.3.
1289: 
1290:   audit                           why it passed
1291:   lattice · equations             neither is a structural or numerical claim
1292:   consistency                     both were internally consistent and cited sections that exist
1293:   artefact                        both rendered correctly
1294:   coherence                       both were well-formed tables with valid references
1295:

{"returncode":0,"stdout":"1226: ### 3.2 The whitespace clause, and two measurements that were wrong
1227:  A gap a reader sees is a defect the source cannot show. So the audit reads the position of every
1228:  glyph and every image and compares the inked extent with the frame.
1229: 
1230:  On this book: median foot gap 3.3%, nine pages above 15%, worst 31% — and that one is the
1231:  end of a section, where a gap is correct. Interior gaps cluster at 16–28%, which is exactly the
1232:  CondPageBreak(58mm) guard that stops a heading landing at the foot of a page.
1233: 
1234:  Tightening the guard makes it worse, not better. At 46mm the count of gaps falls from nine to
1235:  seven and the worst rises from 31% to 43%, because a heading allowed to sit lower pushes the figure
1236:  block after it off the page entirely. 58mm is the optimum, and it was found by measuring rather
1237:  than by preference.
1238: 
1239: ### 3.3 Exhaustive, and what to do when it is impossible
1240:  Check every cell where the set is finite and small enough. Where it is not, state the sampling and its
1241:  size in the same sentence as the result, and never let a sampled figure stand where an exhaustive one
1242:  is affordable — §16.5 stood on 30,000 samples of a 6,912-cell box until register 248.
1243: 
1244: ### 3.4 And two of the audit's own measurements were wrong first
1245:  The first attempt used the PDF text matrix directly and reported a median inked fraction of 103%
1246:  — impossible — with y-coordinates of 5, 6 and −220. The text matrix is not page geometry until it is
1247:  composed with the current transformation matrix.
1248: 
1249:  The second attempt counted characters and not images, and flagged seven pages as having a
1250:  25–45% gap at the head. All seven begin with a figure. The space was not empty; it was occupied by
1251:  something the measurement could not see.
1252: 
1253:     Both are the same error as the audits they were written to replace: a check looking at the
1254:     wrong artefact. An audit is not exempt from the discipline it enforces, and this one needed two
1255:     corrections before its first clean reading.

1261:  is duplicated; nothing in fig/ is unused; and after one correction every figure number matches the

{"returncode":0,"stdout":"1303: ### 3.7 The precedences, and the certificate for the dimension
1304:  §3.8 states nineteen precedences and an order dimension of 2, **and printed neither the precedences nor
1305:  the certificate.** Both are here, so both are checkable.
1306: 
1307:  **The twenty-two.** CELL before LATTICE, since a set containing an invalid cell has no closure worth
1308:  testing. LATTICE before EQUATIONS. CELL before DISTINCTNESS. EQUATIONS before SCOPE, AGREEMENT,
1309:  ARITHMETIC and ENUMERATION, since a property of a number presupposes the number. CONSISTENCY before
1310:  REDUNDANCY, and both before ARTEFACT. MARKUP before ARTEFACT and FIDELITY. ARTEFACT before MEASURE,
1311:  FIDELITY and PROJECTION. ATTRIBUTION before REPRODUCTION. SEQUENCE before ANTECEDENT, COHERENCE and
1312:  PROJECTION. **And INPUT before SCOPE, ARITHMETIC and ENUMERATION** — all three read a result against
1313:  its inputs, and cannot run where the inputs are not printed.
1314: 
1315:  **The order falls into three components** — ten audits, nine, and a pair — and the dimension of a
1316:  disjoint sum is the greatest of its parts. **A dimension is certified by exhibiting two linear
1317:  extensions whose intersection is exactly the order**, which is checkable in a page even though finding
1318:  it is not:
1319: 
1320:   component of nine
1321:    L1  CELL < DISTINCTNESS < LATTICE < EQUATIONS < AGREEMENT < INPUT < SCOPE < ARITHMETIC <
1322:        ENUMERATION
1323:    L2  INPUT < CELL < LATTICE < EQUATIONS < ENUMERATION < ARITHMETIC < SCOPE < AGREEMENT <
1324:        DISTINCTNESS
1325: 
1326:   component of ten
1327:    L1  CONSISTENCY < REDUNDANCY < MARKUP < ARTEFACT < FIDELITY < MEASURE < SEQUENCE < PROJECTION <
1328:        COHERENCE < ANTECEDENT
1329:    L2  SEQUENCE < ANTECEDENT < COHERENCE < MARKUP < CONSISTENCY < REDUNDANCY < ARTEFACT < PROJECTION <
1330:        MEASURE < FIDELITY
1331: 
1332:  **dim(hierarchy) = 2, certified.** The ten-element component has 4,140 linear extensions and two of
1333:  them suffice; the nine-element component has 792 and two suffice.
1334: 
1335:     **A certificate is checkable where a search is not.** Verifying these four lists takes 362
1336:     comparisons; finding them took eight and a half million.
1337: 
1338:  That is the third companion paper's third finding arriving in the book's own instruments: **an arrow
1339:  is a ranking function and a dimension is a realiser, and both are things an analyst supplies rather
1340:  than derives.** Register 377.
1341: 
1342: ### 3.7.1 The twenty-first audit — INPUT
1343:  Registers 376 and 377 found the same defect twice in two turns: **a result stated from data the book
1344:  does not print.** E(audits), then 17, rested on coordinates that were never printed; dim(hierarchy) = 2
1345:  rested on precedences that were never printed. Both were correct and neither was checkable.
1346: 
1347:   21 — INPUT. *Source, itself, unusable, presupposes the claims are individually true.* **Every
1348:   stated result must print the data it was computed from.** Not the computation and not the method —
1349:   the input set, in a form a reader can rerun. A result whose inputs are absent is not wrong; it is
1350:   **unusable**, which is a different cost and the one this coordinate names.
1351: 
1352:  **Its cell was among the seventeen §3.8 leaves admitted and absent**, and adding it takes E(audits)
1353:  from 17 to 16. That is the third of that count confirmed by a defect rather than proposed, after
1354:  SEQUENCE and PROJECTION.
1355: 
1356:  **Why the other twenty could not catch it.** ARITHMETIC and ENUMERATION check a number against a
1357:  computation the book performs; SCOPE checks that a figure carries its frame. **All three presuppose
1358:  the input exists in the text.** A result whose input was never printed passes every one of them,
1359:  because there is nothing for them to disagree with — the same shape as PROJECTION's finding that
1360:  correctness and completeness are different failures.
1361: 
1362:  **First run: nine stated results tested, nine pass** — but only because registers 376 and 377 printed
1363:  the two tables an hour earlier. Run against the book as it stood this morning it would have failed
1364:  twice. Register 379.
1365:

{"returncode":0,"stdout":"1366: ### 3.8 How the set grew, and the two things that held
1367:  Seven audits became twenty across these sessions, each addition written as its own account of why the
1368:  set had been incomplete. Those accounts are one thing said seven times, and it is said once here.
1369: 
1370:   when                     audits   E(audits)   what the gap was, and what closed it
1371:   as first stated               7   11 at 3 coords   the set was closed under self-reference: every
1372:                                                      audit checked the book against the book
1373:   ATTRIBUTION added             7   —                the first outward-pointing check; found four
1374:                                                      works cited and unlisted
1375:   the eleven retained          18   0 at 3 coords    every admitted cell occupied
1376:   DEPTH admitted               18   19 at 4 coords   the hierarchy demanded a fourth coordinate; the
1377:                                                      zero had been cheap
1378:   SEQUENCE added               19   18               a numbering is a claim about position and
1379:                                                      nothing tested it
1380:   PROJECTION added             20   17               a derived list is as complete as its rule, and a
1381:                                                      rule that misses a case fails silently
1382: 
1383:  **Two findings survive the growth and are the reason to keep the record at all.**
1384: 
1385:  **E is relative to its box.** E(audits) read 11, then 0, then 19, then 17 without the audits changing
1386:  — only the coordinates did. §18.4.1 and register 275 carry the general statement: **a zero is worth
1387:  exactly the size of the box it was computed in**, so every E owes both its fibration and its
1388:  coordinate list.
1389: 
1390:  **The hierarchy did not tangle as it grew.** Nineteen precedences hold between the twenty; the
1391:  precedence poset falls into three components; its **order dimension is 2, unchanged from seven audits
1392:  to twenty**. Two coordinates recover which audit runs before which; the other two carry what an audit
1393:  *is*. Order dimension answers §15's S2 and says nothing about S1, and Λ has the same division — eight
1394:  coordinates over an order of dimension seven, the surplus axis being the coupling, which is what
1395:  makes a cell mean rather than sort. Registers 262, 273–276, 285, 294, 295, 309.
1396: 
1397: 
1398: ### 3.9 The audits are run on every output, and the requirement is executable
1399:  §3 defines twenty-two audits and left when to run them as a habit. A habit is not a check. From this
1400:  build onward **every output of this work is audited by all twenty before it is delivered**, and the
1401:  requirement exists as a file rather than an intention: *The Method 1.6 audits.py* runs the whole set
1402:  against the source and the rendered artefact together and exits with the number of failures, so a
1403:  build that has not been audited cannot be mistaken for one that has.
1404: 
1405:  **And three of the twenty-one have never fired, which §4.6 says is not the same as passing.** A check
1406:  must be demonstrated capable of returning a failure before its passing is evidence, and ANTECEDENT,
1407:  ARITHMETIC and REPRODUCTION have caught nothing in this book — no register entry names any of them.
1408:  Each has a constructible failing input and none needs new theory:
1409: 
1410:   audit          the input that must make it fail
1411:   ANTECEDENT     a label used in Chapter 1 and defined in Chapter 32 — a forward reference the
1412:                  source-against-itself read must flag
1413:   ARITHMETIC     a product stated beside its own printed factors and wrong: *33 × 5 = 166* against
1414:                  §12.6.1's table, which prints 33, 5 and 165
1415:   REPRODUCTION   an altered Condon–Shortley term entry, against the microstate enumeration that
1416:                  reproduces ten tables of ten exactly
1417: 
1418:  **Running these three is not optional bookkeeping.** §3.6 records two sections surviving their own
1419:  supersession and passing five audits; §3.4 records the whitespace audit's first two measurements
1420:  being wrong. **An audit that has never returned a failure is indistinguishable from one that
1421:  cannot**, and this book has three. Register 422.
1422: 
1423:  **Why a file and not a rule.** Register 259 records a defect repaired twice and reintroduced in the
1424:  next turn, and §4.4 draws the conclusion: a fix that leaves the mechanism unchanged is an
1425:  instance fix. Every audit in this book was run by hand until now, which made *audited* a claim about
1426:  a session and not a property of an artefact. It is now the second. The script reads the source by
1427:  name, the PDF by name and the press by name, so FIDELITY and PROJECTION compare three files that
1428:  must agree and none of them can be updated alone without the run reporting it.
1429: 
1430:  **What it does not do.** It decides nothing. Every flag it raises is a hypothesis under §4.7 and
1431:  must be localised before it is recorded — four of the last five flags this book has seen were the
1432:  detectors and not the book. And **it cannot audit itself**: the script is an instrument, its own
1433:  correctness is untested by anything in the twenty, and that is a gap this section admits rather than
1434:  closes. Register 300.
1435: 
","stderr":""}

# r2-ch3.py — Phase R2, main Chapter 3 (chat 69). Re-measures every figure of Chapter 3 that is computable
# from what the chapter itself prints: the §2.21 coordinate table (L1116–1138), the §3.7 precedences
# (L1307–1313) and the four linear extensions (L1320–1330). Every line printed is MEASURED; the read decides.
import re, itertools, sys
MAIN = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else '../members94/The_Method_1_6-2.md'
lines = open(MAIN, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
# ---- §2.21 table -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
READS = ['object', 'source', 'artefact', 'outside']
COMP = ['itself', 'other places', 'a computation']
COST = ['wrong', 'unreadable', 'unusable', 'dishonest']
PRES = ['nothing', 'claims individually true', 'also mutually consistent']   # 'labels are addressable' reads as the second (L1143)
rows = {}
for ln in lines[1116:1138]:
    m = re.match(r'\s*(\d+)\s+([A-Z]+)\s+(object|source|artefact|outside)\s+(itself|other places|a computation)\s+(wrong|unreadable|unusable|dishonest)\s+(.+?)\s*$', ln)
    assert m, ln
    no, name, r, c, k, p = m.groups()
    p = 'claims individually true' if p == 'labels are addressable' else p
    rows[int(no)] = (name, (READS.index(r), COMP.index(c), COST.index(k), PRES.index(p)))
assert len(rows) == 22 and [rows[i][0] for i in range(1, 23)] == ['LATTICE','EQUATIONS','CONSISTENCY','REDUNDANCY','ARTEFACT','COHERENCE','ATTRIBUTION','CELL','DISTINCTNESS','SCOPE','ANTECEDENT','MARKUP','AGREEMENT','ARITHMETIC','ENUMERATION','FIDELITY','MEASURE','REPRODUCTION','SEQUENCE','PROJECTION','INPUT','CENSUS']
cells4 = [rows[i][1] for i in range(1, 23)]
print('§2.21 table: 22 rows;', len(set(cells4)), 'distinct 4-cells (L1140 "twenty-two distinct cells, no collision");',
      len(set(c[:3] for c in cells4)), 'distinct 3-cells over 22;',
      len(set(c[:3] for c in cells4[:18])), 'distinct 3-cells over the first 18 (Register L1053 "eighteen audits over seventeen cells")')
# ---- closure operators ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def box(X):
    d = len(next(iter(X))); lo = [min(x[i] for x in X) for i in range(d)]; hi = [max(x[i] for x in X) for i in range(d)]
    return set(itertools.product(*[range(lo[i], hi[i] + 1) for i in range(d)]))
def closure(X):   # the tightest monotone two-variable-bound closure of r2-ch1.py, coordinate-general
    X = set(X); d = len(next(iter(X))); B = box(X)
    lo = [min(x[i] for x in X) for i in range(d)]; hi = [max(x[i] for x in X) for i in range(d)]
    F = {}; G = {}
    for i in range(d):
        for j in range(d):
            if i == j: continue
            for v in range(lo[i], hi[i] + 1):
                le = [x[j] for x in X if x[i] <= v]; ge = [x[j] for x in X if x[i] >= v]
                F[(i, j, v)] = max(le) if le else -1
                G[(i, j, v)] = min(ge) if ge else 10 ** 6
    return {z for z in B if all(G[(i, j, z[i])] <= z[j] <= F[(i, j, z[i])] for i in range(d) for j in range(d) if i != j)}
stages = [('as first stated (1–7)', 7), ('the eleven retained (1–18)', 18), ('SEQUENCE added (1–19)', 19),
          ('PROJECTION added (1–20)', 20), ('INPUT added (1–21)', 21), ('CENSUS added (1–22)', 22)]
print('E(audits) = |closure(X)| − |X| ; printed §3.8 table: 7→11 at 3 coords, 18→0 at 3, 18→19 at 4, 19→18, 20→17; §3.7.1: 21→16; Register L1473: 16')
for label, n in stages:
    X4 = set(cells4[:n]); X3 = set(c[:3] for c in cells4[:n])
    print('  %-28s 3 coords: closure E=%2d box E=%2d | 4 coords: closure E=%2d box E=%3d' % (
        label, len(closure(X3)) - len(X3), len(box(X3)) - len(X3), len(closure(X4)) - len(X4), len(box(X4)) - len(X4)))
X6 = set(cells4[:6]); X6_3 = set(c[:3] for c in cells4[:6])
print('  first six without ATTRIBUTION: 3 coords closure E=%d box E=%d' % (len(closure(X6_3)) - len(X6_3), len(box(X6_3)) - len(X6_3)))
# ---- §3.7 precedences ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
P = [('CELL','LATTICE'),('LATTICE','EQUATIONS'),('CELL','DISTINCTNESS'),
     ('EQUATIONS','SCOPE'),('EQUATIONS','AGREEMENT'),('EQUATIONS','ARITHMETIC'),('EQUATIONS','ENUMERATION'),
     ('CONSISTENCY','REDUNDANCY'),('CONSISTENCY','ARTEFACT'),('REDUNDANCY','ARTEFACT'),
     ('MARKUP','ARTEFACT'),('MARKUP','FIDELITY'),
     ('ARTEFACT','MEASURE'),('ARTEFACT','FIDELITY'),('ARTEFACT','PROJECTION'),
     ('ATTRIBUTION','REPRODUCTION'),
     ('SEQUENCE','ANTECEDENT'),('SEQUENCE','COHERENCE'),('SEQUENCE','PROJECTION'),
     ('INPUT','SCOPE'),('INPUT','ARITHMETIC'),('INPUT','ENUMERATION')]
names = [rows[i][0] for i in range(1, 23)]
print('precedences listed at L1307–1313:', len(P), '(L1304 "nineteen" + INPUT\'s three)')
# components
adj = {n: set() for n in names}
for a, b in P: adj[a].add(b); adj[b].add(a)
seen = set(); comps = []
for n in names:
    if n in seen: continue
    st = [n]; comp = set()
    while st:
        u = st.pop()
        if u in comp: continue
        comp.add(u); st.extend(adj[u] - comp)
    seen |= comp; comps.append(sorted(comp))
print('components of the 22 under the precedences:', sorted(len(c) for c in comps), '; singletons:', [c for c in comps if len(c) == 1],
      '(L1315 "three components — ten audits, nine, and a pair")')
# transitive closure
def tc(P, U):
    R = set(P)
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for (a, b) in list(R):
            for (c, d) in list(R):
                if b == c and (a, d) not in R: R.add((a, d)); changed = True
    return {(a, b) for (a, b) in R if a in U and b in U}
L9a = 'CELL DISTINCTNESS LATTICE EQUATIONS AGREEMENT INPUT SCOPE ARITHMETIC ENUMERATION'.split()
L9b = 'INPUT CELL LATTICE EQUATIONS ENUMERATION ARITHMETIC SCOPE AGREEMENT DISTINCTNESS'.split()
L10a = 'CONSISTENCY REDUNDANCY MARKUP ARTEFACT FIDELITY MEASURE SEQUENCE PROJECTION COHERENCE ANTECEDENT'.split()
L10b = 'SEQUENCE ANTECEDENT COHERENCE MARKUP CONSISTENCY REDUNDANCY ARTEFACT PROJECTION MEASURE FIDELITY'.split()
def pairs(Lst): return {(Lst[i], Lst[j]) for i in range(len(Lst)) for j in range(i + 1, len(Lst))}
def count_ext(U, R):
    U = list(U); idx = {u: i for i, u in enumerate(U)}
    below = {u: {a for (a, b) in R if b == u} for u in U}
    from functools import lru_cache
    @lru_cache(None)
    def f(mask):
        if mask == (1 << len(U)) - 1: return 1
        tot = 0
        for u in U:
            if not mask >> idx[u] & 1 and all(mask >> idx[a] & 1 for a in below[u]): tot += f(mask | 1 << idx[u])
        return tot
    return f(0)
for tag, La, Lb in [('nine', L9a, L9b), ('ten', L10a, L10b)]:
    U = set(La); assert U == set(Lb)
    R = tc(P, U)
    ext_a = R <= pairs(La); ext_b = R <= pairs(Lb)
    inter = pairs(La) & pairs(Lb)
    print('component of %s: L1 is a linear extension: %s; L2: %s; L1∩L2 == the order: %s (order has %d comparable pairs, intersection %d); linear extensions: %d (L1332–1333 "4,140" / "792")'
          % (tag, ext_a, ext_b, inter == R, len(R), len(inter), count_ext(U, R)))
    if inter != R: print('   extra pairs in intersection:', sorted(inter - R), '; missing:', sorted(R - inter))
n9, n10 = 9, 10
print('comparisons: 2·C(9,2)+2·C(10,2) =', 2 * 36 + 2 * 45, '; 4 lists × pairs =', 4 * (36 + 45), '; +2×19 precedences =', 4 * (36 + 45) + 38, '; +2×22 =', 4 * (36 + 45) + 44, '(L1335 "362")')
print('unordered pairs of ten-component extensions: 4140·4139/2 =', 4140 * 4139 // 2, '(L1336 "eight and a half million")')
# at twenty audits (no INPUT, no CENSUS): components and precedence count
P20 = [(a, b) for (a, b) in P if 'INPUT' not in (a, b)]
adj20 = {n: set() for n in names[:20]}
for a, b in P20: adj20[a].add(b); adj20[b].add(a)
seen = set(); sizes = []
for n in names[:20]:
    if n in seen: continue
    st = [n]; comp = set()
    while st:
        u = st.pop()
        if u in comp: continue
        comp.add(u); st.extend(adj20[u] - comp)
    seen |= comp; sizes.append(len(comp))
print('at twenty audits: %d precedences, components %s (L1390–1391 "nineteen precedences … three components")' % (len(P20), sorted(sizes)))

import importlib.util,itertools
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('tower','../members94/tower-2.py'); tw=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(tw)
L=tw.L8(); S=set(L); d=8
def lower_covers(x):
    # cover relation in the product order restricted to Λ8: y<x, no z with y<z<x
    below=[y for y in L if all(a<=b for a,b in zip(y,x)) and y!=x]
    return [y for y in below if not any(all(a<=b for a,b in zip(y,z)) and all(a<=b for a,b in zip(z,x)) and z!=y and z!=x for z in below)]
J=[x for x in L if len(lower_covers(x))==1]

le=lambda a,b: all(u<=v for u,v in zip(a,b))

w=0;best=None
for r in range(1,len(J)+1):
    found=False
    for A in itertools.combinations(J,r):
        if all(not le(a,b) and not le(b,a) for a,b in itertools.combinations(A,2)): w=r;best=A;found=True;break
    if not found: break

# min chain partition (Dilworth) via greedy check that a partition into w chains exists: use bipartite matching
Jl=list(J);n=len(Jl)
adj={i:[j for j in range(n) if i!=j and le(Jl[i],Jl[j])] for i in range(n)}
match=[-1]*n
def aug(u,seen):
    for v in adj[u]:
        if v in seen: continue
        seen.add(v)
        if match[v]==-1 or aug(match[v],seen): match[v]=u; return True
    return False
m=sum(aug(u,set()) for u in range(n))

print('join/meet closed:',all(tuple(map(max,a,b)) in S and tuple(map(min,a,b)) in S for a in J for b in J))

# READ-ch3 — Phase R2, main volume Chapter 3 "The twenty-two prime audits, ordered by what a failure costs" (chat 69, continued past the false close)

Member The_Method_1_6-2.md (BUILD90 main, md5 4aef772b…), L1003–L1435 (433 lines, 28,498 characters), read in full against (i) each cited section, (ii) each cited Register entry (248, 259, 262, 273–276, 285, 294, 295, 300, 309, 374, 376, 377, 379, 415, 422, 439, 506, 514, resolved to their headlines by `^### N`), (iii) the chapter's own printed inputs recomputed — the §2.21 coordinate table, the §3.7 precedences and the four linear extensions (r2-ch3.py, banked beside tower-2.py), (iv) the rebuilt Λ8 for the one lattice claim (L1394). Labels: MEASURED = produced by the named command or instrument; INFERRED = my reading; record-carried = a figure the record states and no instrument here can reproduce. Form follows SWEEP-B-C-chat67.md (site · PRINTED · SOURCE · label · READING). Nothing in any volume was changed.

Correction to READ-ch2-A item on §2.21/§2.22 and READ-ch2-B on the same: both said no §2.21/§2.22 heading exists. Wrong. The headings exist at L1081 and L1145, inside Chapter 3 (3-02 below). The finding about the book is the misplacement, not the absence.

## A. Deviations (both texts)

**3-01 · L1004 (chapter lead).** PRINTED: `Every session closes with twenty-two audits. They are not spot checks, and they are not equal. They` — the line ends there; L1005 blank; L1006 is the §3.0 heading. MEASURED (awk). READING: a sentence lost at "They".

**3-02 · L1081, L1145, L1148, L1184 (placement).** PRINTED: `### 2.21 A figure removed must have its data represented another way`, `### 2.22 A corroborable entry …`, `### 2.23 A closed index must be stated by its expression …`, `### 2.24 Never one heuristic — §2.8 …` — four Chapter 2 sections between §3.0 (L1006) and §3.1 (L1219). SOURCE: §2.20 ends at L1002; §5's table (L1500–1501) and L7809 cite §2.21/§2.22; Register 514 counts twenty-four protocols. MEASURED (heading map `^#`). READING: the sections belong before L1003; the chapter as printed is §3.0, §2.21–§2.24, §3.1–§3.9.

**3-03 · L1145–L1147 (§2.22).** PRINTED: the heading and two blank lines; no body. SOURCE: the requirement §2.22's title names is printed at §2.23 L1166–1168 (`Any register entry that a proof … settles must name that object, and the object must name the entry. A reference in one direction is a citation; a reference in both is an index`) with its evidence at L1170–1182 and Register 415 (L1545: `§2.22 states the requirement in both directions`). MEASURED (awk, grep). READING: §2.22's text has migrated into §2.23; §2.22 is an empty section cited by the Register and §5. — INFERRED as to the migration.

**3-04 · L1034 against the table L1116–1138; L1036–1038, L1066, L1077–1079.** PRINTED L1034: `The twenty-two are ordered by the cost of the failure each one catches.` The cost column of the table reads, in row order: wrong, wrong, unreadable, unreadable, unusable, unusable, dishonest, wrong, wrong, wrong, unreadable, unusable, wrong, unreadable, unusable, unusable, unusable, dishonest, unusable, unusable, unusable, wrong. MEASURED (r2-ch3.py, table parse). L1036–1038 order `The first two … The next two … The next two … The seventh` and L1077–1079 `it is the only one of the seven that cannot be run by reading the book` describe seven; L1066 marks COHERENCE (audit 6) `Last`. READING: the ordering claim is true of audits 1–7 and false of 8–22; the three passages are the seven-audit text under a twenty-two heading.

**3-05 · L1112 and L1140 (the coordinate table).** PRINTED L1112: `The twenty, with their coordinates.` over a table of twenty-two rows; L1140: `Twenty-two audits over twenty-two distinct cells, no collision.` MEASURED (r2-ch3.py): 22 rows, **21 distinct 4-cells** — row 22 CENSUS `source · itself · wrong · claims individually true` is identical to row 10 SCOPE. READING: L1140 is false as printed; CENSUS was added on an occupied cell, which is also why E(audits) does not move when it is added (3-16).

**3-06 · L1160.** PRINTED: `the audits at three coordinates` (one of the twenty closed indices). SOURCE: L1113 `these four values per audit`; L1376 `the hierarchy demanded a fourth coordinate`; Register 275 (L1057). MEASURED (text). READING: the three-coordinate audit index is the state before Register 275; stale.

**3-07 · L1170–L1173 (arithmetic).** PRINTED: `Of 219 entry-lines carrying 248 numbers: 66 carry a mathematical object and a § reference; 89 carry an object and no reference; 35 are mathematical in subject and carry neither; 59 are narrative … 107 entries are corroborable and not searchable`. MEASURED: 66 + 89 + 35 + 59 = 249, not 219 and not 248. SOURCE: Register 415 (L1545) prints 89, 35, `107 of 219 entry lines`, 132, four — and no 248, 66 or 59. READING: the four classes do not partition the 219; 66, 59 and 248 have no source in the Register.

**3-08 · L1082, L1093–L1098 (§F.3.1 pointer).** PRINTED: `§F.3.1 replaces a count with the constraint that generates it — definition = stated forbids inputs = enumerated`; `§F.3.1 names the nine combinations admitted and absent in every state of the book, against a count that read five different values in one session`. SOURCE: §F.3.1 = L11301 `The closure, represented as it must be` (L11301–11400): no `nine combinations`, no `forbids`, no `enumerated`, no `assignment rules` (L1095 is the only site of that phrase in the volume). MEASURED (grep). READING: the pointer resolves to the heading and not to either claim.

**3-09 · L1099–L1100 (§E.1.3).** PRINTED: `§E.1.3 asserts E(Q) = 0 under its fibration, which has held at five different item totals`. SOURCE: §E.1.3 L10976–10977 `E(Q) = 0 under the fibration by domain` — resolves; `five different item totals` has no site in the volume (grep: L1100 only). MEASURED. READING: first half resolves; second half unsourced.

**3-10 · L1264–L1265 (figure numbers).** PRINTED: `Figures 23.1 and 23.2 appeared in the wrong order — the arity figure sits in §30.3.2 and the step-law figure in §30.3.4`. SOURCE: §30.3.2 (L8417) carries `![Figure 30.1]` at L8444; §30.3.4 (L8476) carries `![Figure 30.2]` at L8493; `![Figure 23.1]`/`![Figure 23.2]` exist at L6191/L6193 in Chapter 23. MEASURED (grep). READING: the two figures are now 30.1 and 30.2 — INFERRED from position; L1264 keeps their pre-renumbering labels, against L1261–1262 in the same section (`every figure number matches the chapter it sits in`).

**3-11 · L1258, L1269–L1272 (figure count).** PRINTED: `Twenty-eight figures, each checked against its caption and its file`; dpi rows 5 + 8 + 15 = 28, median 164 dpi. SOURCE: the volume carries 32 distinct `![Figure N.M]` images (grep, sort -u); second site for the finding at Appendix C.3 L10290 (`164 dpi`). MEASURED. READING: 28 is the count at the audit's date; four figures since; the sentence is present-tense.

**3-12 · L1285 (Q's eight items) — cross-chapter, recorded, deferred.** PRINTED: `A summary table listed Q's eight items while Appendix E enumerated, indexed and closed them`. SOURCE: Appendix E L10899 `fourteen items, ten open`; L8794 (Chapter 32 opening) and L11107 (Appendix E) still print `eight items`. MEASURED (grep). READING: L1285 is history and stands; L8794/L11107 are live and belong to the Chapter 32 and Appendix E reads.

**3-13 · L1307, L1315 (precedences, components).** PRINTED: `**The twenty-two.**` heading a list naming twenty-one audits; `The order falls into three components — ten audits, nine, and a pair`. MEASURED (r2-ch3.py): 22 precedences over 21 names; components of the twenty-two under them: sizes 1, 2, 9, 10 — CENSUS appears in no precedence and is a component of its own. READING: three components is true of twenty-one, false of the twenty-two the heading names.

**3-14 · L1304, L1335–L1336 (counts of the certificate).** PRINTED: `§3.8 states nineteen precedences`; `Verifying these four lists takes 362 comparisons; finding them took eight and a half million`. MEASURED: nineteen + INPUT's three = the 22 listed; 4 lists × (36 + 45) pairs + 2 × 19 precedences = 362, and + 2 × 22 = 368; 4,140 × 4,139 / 2 = 8,567,730. READING: 362 was counted with nineteen precedences, the lists it verifies carry twenty-two — INFERRED decomposition, MEASURED arithmetic; "eight and a half million" reproduces.

**3-15 · L1371–L1374 (§3.8 table, first two rows).** PRINTED: `as first stated · 7 · 11 at 3 coords` then `ATTRIBUTION added · 7 · —`. SOURCE: Register 262 (L1017) `A SEVENTH PRIME AUDIT, ATTRIBUTION … The six existing audits were closed under self-reference`; Register 273 (L1049) `E(audits) = 11`. MEASURED (r2-ch3.py): E = 11 at three coordinates for the seven including ATTRIBUTION; E = 10 for the six without. READING: the first row's count already includes ATTRIBUTION; the row that adds it changes nothing; the table's order is not the Register's.

**3-16 · L1367, L1370–L1381, L1352–L1353 (the set's size).** PRINTED L1367: `Seven audits became twenty`; the table ends `PROJECTION added · 20 · 17`. SOURCE: §3.7.1 L1352–1353 `adding it takes E(audits) from 17 to 16`; Register 379 (INPUT, twenty-first); L1138 row 22 CENSUS; L1003/L1399 `twenty-two`; Register L1473 `E(audits) = 16`. MEASURED (r2-ch3.py, the seated closure operator of r2-ch1.py applied to the table): E(audits) = 11 (7 at 3 coords), 0 (18 at 3), 19 (18 at 4), 18 (19), 17 (20), 16 (21), **16 (22)** — every printed value reproduces exactly; the twenty-second leaves E at 16 (3-05). READING: the table stops two audits short; E(audits) for the current set is printed nowhere.

**3-17 · L1385.** PRINTED: `E(audits) read 11, then 0, then 19, then 17 without the audits changing`. SOURCE: the table L1370–1381 four lines above prints 11, 0, 19, 18, 17. MEASURED (text). READING: 18 dropped; the same section disagrees with itself (and with L858, closed as census 675).

**3-18 · L1376 (the coordinate's name).** PRINTED: `DEPTH admitted · 18 · 19 at 4 coords · the hierarchy demanded a fourth coordinate`. SOURCE: the table L1116 heads the fourth column `presupposes`; DEPTH is the name at L5025 and Register 275 (L1057); the word DEPTH does not occur in §2.21. MEASURED (grep). READING: one coordinate under two names — INFERRED identity.

**3-19 · L1390–L1391.** PRINTED: `Nineteen precedences hold between the twenty; the precedence poset falls into three components; its order dimension is 2, unchanged from seven audits to twenty`. MEASURED (r2-ch3.py) at twenty (no INPUT, no CENSUS): 19 precedences, components of sizes 2, 8, 10 — three; the ten-component certificate holds; the nine-component certificate printed at L1320–1324 includes INPUT. READING: true of twenty; the chapter is headed twenty-two.

**3-20 · L1393–L1395.** PRINTED: `Λ has the same division — eight coordinates over an order of dimension seven, the surplus axis being the coupling`. SOURCE: Mathematical Compendium L1472–1474 `Order dimension (Dushnik–Miller) … order dimension of Λ₈ is 7 = width of J(Λ), certified both ways`; no pointer at L1394; Register 35 (L211–213) `THE ORDER DIMENSION OF Λ IS EXACTLY THREE` is the Λ ⊆ ℕ³ of that date (`Since Λ ⊆ ℕ³ … three coordinate projections`). MEASURED (r2-ch3 session code on tower-2.py): |J(Λ8)| = 17, width(J) = 7 (largest antichain), minimum chain partition 7 (Dilworth by matching), Λ8 closed under join and meet. READING: the claim holds; its certificate lives in the compendium unpointed (R-ATTR); Register 35 is a different object and should not be read against it.

**3-21 · L1399, L1400, L1405, L1433 (§3.9).** PRINTED: `§3 defines twenty-two audits`; `every output of this work is audited by all twenty`; `three of the twenty-one have never fired`; `untested by anything in the twenty`. MEASURED (text). READING: three sizes in one section.

**3-22 · L1423–L1425.** PRINTED: `Register 259 records a defect repaired twice and reintroduced in the next turn, and §4.4 draws the conclusion: a fix that leaves the mechanism unchanged is an instance fix`. SOURCE: 259 has no `### 259`; it sits in the grouped heading `### 203, 215, 218, 259, 280, 283, 284, 286, 291` (Register L1319, `§4.2 — WROTE INTO A STRUCTURE WITHOUT READING IT`); §4.4 is the plain-line item L1445 `a count kept by judgement — read the list; do not carry the number`; `instance fix` is printed at L7804 and L7820 (§28.7.8 region) and L1425. MEASURED (grep). READING: the §4.4 pointer does not reach the conclusion attributed to it; Register 259's individual content is not recoverable from the group.

**3-23 · L1205, L1405, L1424, L1430 (§4.x pointers).** PRINTED: `§4.6's condition`, `§4.6 says`, `§4.4 draws`, `a hypothesis under §4.7`. SOURCE: Chapter 4 (L1436–1464) has no `###` headings; 4.1–4.10 are plain-line items at L1441–1451. §4.6 L1447 `a test that could not fail — exhibit the failure mode before trusting the pass` and §4.7 L1448 `a flag is a hypothesis — localise a detector's output` match their uses. MEASURED (awk, grep `§4\.`: §4.1 ×1, §4.2 ×1, §4.4 ×1, §4.6 ×7, §4.7 ×1 in the volume). READING: same class as READ-ch1's plain-line sub-headings; §4.4 see 3-22.

**3-24 · L1338–L1340.** PRINTED: `the third companion paper's third finding … an arrow is a ranking function and a dimension is a realiser`. SOURCE: the third companion paper is *On the Matter of Time Travel* (References L11604–11605; §D.5.8 L10757); neither `ranking function` nor `realiser` occurs in the members Transitions.md / INTEGRATION-transitions.md; `realiser` in the volume at L1339, L5029, L5036. MEASURED (grep). READING: the paper resolves; the finding is record-carried.

**3-25 · L1373 against L1221.** PRINTED L1373: `found four works cited and unlisted`; L1221–1223: `the three precedents that place this book's central theorem in existing literature were cited in the text and absent from the References … 262`. SOURCE: L71 (front matter) prints `four works cited`. MEASURED (grep). READING: four and three may be different quantities (works vs precedents) — INFERRED; the chapter does not say so.

**3-26 · L1415–L1416.** PRINTED: `the microstate enumeration that reproduces ten tables of ten exactly`. SOURCE: `ten tables` has one site in the volume; microstate enumeration is defined at L3060. MEASURED (grep). READING: record-carried.

**3-27 · §3.2 L1230–1237, §3.4 L1245–1251 (PDF geometry).** PRINTED: `median foot gap 3.3%, nine pages above 15%, worst 31%`, `16–28%`, `CondPageBreak(58mm)`, `At 46mm … nine to seven … 31% to 43%`, `median inked fraction of 103%`, `y-coordinates of 5, 6 and −220`, `seven pages … 25–45% gap`. SOURCE: no second site for any of them (grep `median foot`, `103%`, `58mm`: this section only). MEASURED (grep). READING: record-carried; not reproducible without the built PDF.

**3-28 · L1431, L1362.** PRINTED: `four of the last five flags this book has seen were the detectors and not the book` (one site; record-carried); `nine stated results tested, nine pass` — Register 379 (L1405) `nine pass … fails twice` resolves. MEASURED (grep).

**3-29 · L1063.** PRINTED: `*Source, other places, unusable, presupposes labels are addressable.*` as the second sentence of the COHERENCE paragraph. SOURCE: the table row 6 (L1122) `COHERENCE · source · other places · unusable · labels are addressable`. MEASURED. READING: the audit's coordinate tuple printed unlabelled inside its prose (L1347 prints INPUT's the same way, labelled by position only).

**3-30 · L1401.** PRINTED: `the requirement exists as a file rather than an intention: *The Method 1.6 audits.py* runs the whole set`. SOURCE: one site in the volume; no member of either bundle is named audits.py (members carrying `audit`: IOI_SPEC_AUDIT.md, MAIN_AUDIT.md, MATH_AUDIT.md, PHYS_AUDIT.md, REGISTER_AUDIT.md, tb_audit.py); Register 300 (L1125) records the executable set. MEASURED (ls, grep). READING: the file the sentence rests on is not in the bundle; whether it should be is M's.

**3-31 · Layout.** Column dumps (space-aligned tables) at L1010–1019, L1116–1138, L1269–1272, L1290–1294, L1320–1330, L1370–1381, L1410–1416; four-space-indented paragraphs (rendered as code blocks by Markdown) at L1021–1022, L1030–1032, L1036–1038, L1077–1079, L1087–1089, L1150–1152, L1166–1168, L1179–1180, L1186–1188, L1213–1214, L1253–1255, L1279–1280, L1296–1298, L1335–1336; double blank at L1396–1397. MEASURED. Same class as READ-ch1/ch2 layout items.

## B. Verified (claim and source agree; instrument where one exists)

- L1008–1019 ten index audits (1, 2, 8, 9, 10, 13, 14, 18, 20, 21) and L1024–1026 twelve artefact audits: 10 + 12 = 22 names, matching the table's twenty-two. MEASURED.
- L1042 `475,800 pairs` = C(976, 2). MEASURED (r2-ch1).
- Register 274 (L1053) `eighteen audits over seventeen cells`: the first 18 rows give 17 distinct three-coordinate cells. MEASURED (r2-ch3.py).
- L1371–1381 and L1352–1353: E(audits) 11 / 0 / 19 / 18 / 17 / 16 all reproduce under the seated closure operator (3-16). MEASURED.
- L1320–1330: both pairs of linear extensions are linear extensions of their component and intersect to exactly the component's order (19 comparable pairs each) — dim ≤ 2 certified; neither component is a chain, so dim = 2. L1332–1333: 792 and 4,140 linear extensions, exact. MEASURED (r2-ch3.py).
- L1352 `seventeen §3.8 leaves admitted and absent` = E at twenty; L1356 `the other twenty` = 21 − 1. MEASURED.
- L1394 order dimension seven of Λ8: width(J(Λ8)) = 7 = minimum chain partition (3-20). MEASURED.
- L1208–1210 `12, 7, 7, 7 and 40`, spread thirty-three, exact seven: §14.5.9 table L3929 `976 · 12 · 7 · 7 · 7 · 40 · 5 · 7 · 33`; Register 506 (L1889) same figures; L1203 `twelve cycles` at L3935. MEASURED (grep).
- L1242 `§16.5 stood on 30,000 samples of a 6,912-cell box until register 248`: §16.5 L4455–4456 and Register 248 (L981) agree; the box of Λ8 is 6,912 (r2-ch2). MEASURED.
- L1413–1414 `§12.6.1's table, which prints 33, 5 and 165`: L2367 row `0 · 33 · 5 · 165 · 165`. MEASURED (grep).
- L1150 `§15.2 proves those envelopes are recoverable`: §15.2 L4286–4290 `S3 says the envelopes are recoverable from the cells … ℛ(Λ) = Λ exactly. Always succeeds`. MEASURED (grep).
- L1155/L1163 §2.18 = L840 `What is computable, and what is decided`; L1190–1193 §2.8 = L607 `Two independent routes`, both quoted sentences present (L608, L615). MEASURED.
- L1069–1073 ATTRIBUTION's five checks: §29.2 owner column (L7878), Appendix D `precedent found` (one site), Appendix B §B.1 Sources. MEASURED (grep).
- L1102–1105 press readouts: L8862, L8976 (Chapter 32); Register L1389. MEASURED (grep).
- L1161 `the tower states its five bounds`: tower-2.py has five stages beyond Λ8. MEASURED.
- L1220 `twenty-eight cross-references`: second site L76. L1276 Appendix C.3 = L10283 `What was inherited and not recomputed`, `164 dpi` at L10290. L1223 §28.7.8 = L7684 `The recurring mechanisms, grouped`. L1288 §E.5 = L11143, §30.3 = L8399. L1300–1301 Chapter 32 opens (L8794) on Appendix E's closed index. L1386 §18.4.1 = L4999, `A zero is worth the size of the box` at L5075 within it. MEASURED (grep).
- Register headlines resolve to their uses: 262 (ATTRIBUTION seventh), 273 (E = 11), 275 (DEPTH, zero worth its box), 276 (dim = 2), 285 (SEQUENCE nineteenth), 294 (PROJECTION twentieth), 295 (hierarchy restated at twenty; the misread coordinate = `labels are addressable reading as the second`), 300 (executable set), 309 (condensed by mechanism), 374 (§2.21 protocol), 376 (coordinates printed), 377 (dimension certificate), 379 (INPUT twenty-first; nine pass), 415 (89 / 35 / 107 of 219 / 132 / four), 422 (three audits never fired), 439 (expression vs verdict), 506, 514 (twenty-four protocols, §2.24 = §2.8). MEASURED (`^### N`, headline printed).
- L1405–1407 `no register entry names any of them`: capitalised ANTECEDENT occurs in the Register at L1197 (a heading placement entry, not a catch) and L1573 (422 itself); ARITHMETIC and REPRODUCTION after L1573 occur only as ordinary words (L2321, L2373, L2969, L4941 …). MEASURED (grep `\b[A-Z]+\b`). Holds.
- L1158–1159 fourteen + one + five = twenty. MEASURED arithmetic; the classification is record-carried.

## C. Incidental

- L1030–1031 `All twenty-two run on every build` against L1400 `audited by all twenty` (3-21).
- The E(audits) for the first six audits (before ATTRIBUTION) is 10 under the closure; the book never printed it. MEASURED, noted only.
- CENSUS's coordinates duplicate SCOPE's (3-05); if CENSUS is to occupy its own cell the choice of coordinate is subject matter — M's.
- §2.24 states its object as "the seed"; §14.5.7–14.5.9 resolve (headings L3808, L3810, L3917). The seed's exactness (seven) is not re-derived here — it belongs to the Chapter 14 read.

Period and group locate an element; they do not encode why period 1 has room for two elements and period 4 for eighteen. content.text:
{"returncode":0,"stdout":"1613:   the periodic table                                      90      36     no
1614: 
1615:  **The nuclide row names a drawn band and not a measurement, and the distinction is the whole of
1616:  §6.1.** A chart drawn between two monotone drip lines has E = 0, and it has E = 0 **necessarily**:
1617:  ℛ is idempotent — §32.4.1 proves it — so ℛ(X) satisfies ℛℛ(X) = ℛ(X) for any X whatever. **A band's
1618:  closure is a theorem, not a finding about nuclei.** Reporting it beside the calendar's seven, which
1619:  is a measurement, put a tautology and an observation in the same column.
1620: 
1621:  **The measurement is the other object, and it does not close.** Taking the particle-bound nuclides
1622:  themselves over Z ≤ 9 — the chart as nature draws it rather than as a textbook does — gives
1623:  **E = 9**, and the nine cells are named:
1624: 
1625:     He-5, He-7, Li-10, Be-8, Be-13, B-9, B-16, B-18, C-21
1626: 
1627:  Every one is a known unbound nuclide sitting inside the band its own neighbours define. And the band
1628:  is exactly ℛ of the measurement: **the drawn chart is the closure of the real one**, which is why
1629:  the two were conflated and why the conflation is worth the entry.
1630: 
1631:  **What the nine are is content the coordinates cannot carry.** Be-8 is unbound because it is two
1632:  alpha particles and nothing else — clustering. He-5, He-7, Li-10 and Be-13 are unbound by one
1633:  neutron against an even-paired core — pairing. (Z, N) knows how many protons and neutrons a nuclide
1634:  has and cannot know that four of them prefer to be an alpha, or that the last one is unpaired.
1635:  **The nine cells are the pairing and clustering terms of the mass formula, counted.** That is the
1636:  same shape as the calendar's seven and the periodic table's thirty-six: a defect that names a real
1637:  mechanism the index has no axis for. Register 298.
1638: 
1639:  **And the same shape appears a third time, in chemistry, where it can be watched arriving.** An index
1640:  may bracket a quantity only along an axis the quantity is monotone on. Give first ionization energies
1641:  to that test as bare numbers, with no shell model attached:
1642: 
1643:   period 2   Li 5.392  Be 9.323  B 8.298  C 11.260  N 14.534  O 13.618  F 17.423  Ne 21.565
1644:   period 3   Na 5.139  Mg 7.646  Al 5.986  Si 8.152  P 10.487  S 10.360  Cl 12.968  Ar 15.760
1645: 
1646:  **Monotonicity fails at Be→B and N→O, and again at Mg→Al and P→S** — the same two positions in both
1647:  periods. Those are the s² → p¹ subshell opening and the p³ → p⁴ first pairing: the two anomalies every
1648:  general chemistry course teaches, located from the numbers alone. Twelve interior cells, four steps
1649:  refused, **67% admissible**.
1650: 
1651:  It is a retrodiction and not a discovery — both have been explained since the 1920s. What earns it a
1652:  place here is that it is *mechanical*: **where an index refuses, a mechanism is entering that the
1653:  coordinates do not carry**, and the refusal map says where without being told what. The periodic
1654:  table's thirty-six, the measured nuclide chart's nine, and these four are one phenomenon counted in
1655:  three subjects — shell structure, pairing and clustering, subshell opening and pairing again.
1656:  Register 308.
1657: 
1658:  **And a ninth subject entered this book without a coordinate being added to it: time.** Every subject
1659:  above is a thing indexed. Time is not — §F.4.3 records that a date must never enter Λ, since a
1660:  transition is a type and types are not dated, and §12.11.0 shows what enters instead: **composition.**
1661:  An order between cells rather than a stamp on one.
1662: 
1663:  What makes it a subject rather than a metaphor is that it is measured. **Occupancy never rises along
1664:  composition** — zero of 739 steps — so the index has a direction it was not given. The object graph
1665:  falls into three eras pure in occupancy, circulation is total inside each and impossible between them,
1666:  and 904 of 1,654 cells are conservative. **The clock is a coordinate the book already had, read as an
1667:  order.**
1668: 
1669:     Time is the one subject here the index did not have to be extended to reach. It was
1670:     already carrying it, in the constraint that says you cannot place more than you removed.
1671: 
1672:  And it is the subject that most sharply states the method's limit. §12.11.0.1 shows **definability is
1673:  not reachability** — a cell is its own seventeen-bit description and reaches 24.7% of the object, the
1674:  two orders sharing 0.4% of what either carries. An index can say completely what a thing *is* and
1675:  almost nothing about what it can *become*. Register 348.
1676: 
1677:  The calendar's seven are (2,29), (2,30), (2,31), (4,31), (6,31), (9,31) and (11,31).
1678: 
1679:  **That is the content of *Thirty days hath September*.** The rhyme exists because the calendar's coordinates cannot carry the month lengths, and the rhyme is exactly seven cells long.
1680: 
1681: ### 6.2.1 The nuclide chart's defect, recomputed under variation
1682:  §6.2 reports E = 9 on the measured chart at one cutoff. **The measurement is stated here to F.3's
1683:  highest standard** — the method named with its input set, the inputs printed, and the result
1684:  recomputed at four proton-number cutoffs rather than once.
1685: 
1686:  **The method.** Take the measured nuclides as cells (Z, N), close under the monotone envelopes of
1687:  §6.1, and count what the closure admits and the chart lacks. **The input set is the chart itself**,
1688:  printed at §6.2 for Z ≤ 9, and the variation is the cutoff.
1689: 
1690:   Z ≤     nuclides   admitted    E    the cells admitted and absent
1691:   5             27         33    6    He-5, He-7, Li-10, Be-8, Be-13, B-9
1692:   6             40         48    8    …and B-16, B-18
1693:   7             52         61    **9**    …and C-21
1694:   9             80         89    **9**    unchanged
1695: 
1696:     **Every cell named at one cutoff persists at every larger one, and none is added after Z ≤ 7.**
1697:     The defect is not an artefact of where the chart was cut.
1698: 
1699:  That matters because a closure defect measured once can always be blamed on the boundary. **Here the
1700:  boundary was moved four times and the nine cells did not move**, so they are a property of the
1701:  measurement rather than of the window — and each of the nine is a real nuclide the chart omits because
1702:  it is unbound, which is pairing and clustering, mechanisms the two coordinates cannot carry. Registers
1703:  388, 390.
1704: 
1705: ### 6.3 The calendar can be repaired, and the repair is instructive
1706:  The calendar fails for one reason: days(m) is not monotone in m, because February has 28. Relabel the
1707:  months in order of length — February, April, June, September, November, January, March, … — and E
1708:  drops to 0. The 365 cells are identical; only the labels move.
1709: 
1710:  **And the repaired calendar is useless.** A calendar whose months run in order of length is self-defining and unusable.
1711: 
1712:  So the trade is explicit, and it has a number:
1713: 
1714:       E(X) = 7 is the price of keeping January first.
1715: 
1716:  Non-closure is not always a fault. It is sometimes a purchase — usability bought with definitional self-sufficiency. What this book supplies is the price tag, not the verdict.
1717: 
1718: ### 6.4 What follows
1719:  Λ is the same 118 elements on different coordinates, with E = 0. It adds no physics. What it removes is
1720:  the thirty-six.
1721:

1615:  **The nuclide row names a drawn band and not a measurement, and the distinction is the whole of
1616:  §6.1.** A chart drawn between two monotone drip lines has E = 0, and it has E = 0 **necessarily**:
1617:  ℛ is idempotent — §32.4.1 proves it — so ℛ(X) satisfies ℛℛ(X) = ℛ(X) for any X whatever. **A band's
1618:  closure is a theorem, not a finding about nuclei.** Reporting it beside the calendar's seven, which
1619:  is a measurement, put a tautology and an observation in the same column.
1620: 
1621:  **The measurement is the other object, and it does not close.** Taking the particle-bound nuclides
1622:  themselves over Z ≤ 9 — the chart as nature draws it rather than as a textbook does — gives
1623:  **E = 9**, and the nine cells are named:
1624: 
1625:     He-5, He-7, Li-10, Be-8, Be-13, B-9, B-16, B-18, C-21
1626: 
1627:  Every one is a known unbound nuclide sitting inside the band its own neighbours define. And the band
1628:  is exactly ℛ of the measurement: **the drawn chart is the closure of the real one**, which is why
1629:  the two were conflated and why the conflation is worth the entry.
1630: 
1631:  **What the nine are is content the coordinates cannot carry.** Be-8 is unbound because it is two
1632:  alpha particles and nothing else — clustering. He-5, He-7, Li-10 and Be-13 are unbound by one
1633:  neutron against an even-paired core — pairing. (Z, N) knows how many protons and neutrons a nuclide
1634:  has and cannot know that four of them prefer to be an alpha, or that the last one is unpaired.
1635:  **The nine cells are the pairing and clustering terms of the mass formula, counted.** That is the
1636:  same shape as the calendar's seven and the periodic table's thirty-six: a defect that names a real
1637:  mechanism the index has no axis for. Register 298.
1638: 
1639:  **And the same shape appears a third time, in chemistry, where it can be watched arriving.** An index
1640:  may bracket a quantity only along an axis the quantity is monotone on. Give first ionization energies
1641:  to that test as bare numbers, with no shell model attached:
1642: 
1643:   period 2   Li 5.392  Be 9.323  B 8.298  C 11.260  N 14.534  O 13.618  F 17.423  Ne 21.565
1644:   period 3   Na 5.139  Mg 7.646  Al 5.986  Si 8.152  P 10.487  S 10.360  Cl 12.968  Ar 15.760
1645: 
1646:  **Monotonicity fails at Be→B and N→O, and again at Mg→Al and P→S** — the same two positions in both
1647:  periods. Those are the s² → p¹ subshell opening and the p³ → p⁴ first pairing: the two anomalies every
1648:  general chemistry course teaches, located from the numbers alone. Twelve interior cells, four steps
1649:  refused, **67% admissible**.
1650: 
1651:  It is a retrodiction and not a discovery — both have been explained since the 1920s. What earns it a
1652:  place here is that it is *mechanical*: **where an index refuses, a mechanism is entering that the
1653:  coordinates do not carry**, and the refusal map says where without being told what. The periodic
1654:  table's thirty-six, the measured nuclide chart's nine, and these four are one phenomenon counted in
1655:  three subjects — shell structure, pairing and clustering, subshell opening and pairing again.
1656:  Register 308.

1659:  above is a thing indexed. Time is not — §F.4.3 records that a date must never enter Λ, since a
1660:  transition is a type and types are not dated, and §12.11.0 shows what enters instead: **composition.**

1664:  composition** — zero of 739 steps — so the index has a direction it was not given. The object graph
1665:  falls into three eras pure in occupancy, circulation is total inside each and impossible between them,
1666:  and 904 of 1,654 cells are conservative. **The clock is a coordinate the book already had, read as an
1667:  order.**

1669:     Time is the one subject here the index did not have to be extended to reach. It was
1670:     already carrying it, in the constraint that says you cannot place more than you removed.

1673:  not reachability** — a cell is its own seventeen-bit description and reaches 24.7% of the object, the
1674:  two orders sharing 0.4% of what either carries. An index can say completely what a thing *is* and
1675:  almost nothing about what it can *become*. Register 348.

1684:  recomputed at four proton-number cutoffs rather than once.

1687:  §6.1, and count what the closure admits and the chart lacks. **The input set is the chart itself**,
1688:  printed at §6.2 for Z ≤ 9, and the variation is the cutoff.
